hypothesis: A/(A+xi) converges to ln(phi) = 0.4812 under parameter tuning

F1_structural_proximity.description: A/(A+xi) robustly stays within ~2-3% of ln(phi) across all tested coupling and decay parameters
F1_structural_proximity.detail: Mean ratio 0.47-0.49 across coupling [0.5,1.0] and decay_ratio [0.5,2.0]. ln(phi) within 95% CI at every configuration.

F2_convergence_to_ln_phi.description: A/(A+xi) -> ln(phi) as theta -> 0 (perfect coupling limit)
F2_convergence_to_ln_phi.detail: At perfect coupling (c=1.0), mean ratio = 0.469 (2.5% BELOW ln(phi)). Theta crosses zero at c~0.95 but ratio does not equal ln(phi) there.

F3_golden_ratio_in_decay.description: flip_decay/corr_decay = phi gives optimal ln(phi) match
F3_golden_ratio_in_decay.detail: Coarse sampling artifact from exp_19. Fine-resolution exp_20 shows monotonically increasing ratio with decay_ratio. phi is not special.

F4_variance_dominates.description: Per-seed variance (std~0.05) dominates any systematic parameter effects
F4_variance_dominates.detail: Individual seed ratios range 0.39-0.60. Running mean wobbles within +/-0.01 of ln(phi). SE(30 seeds) ~ 0.009, comparable to any systematic offset.

conclusions: ln(phi) is a STRUCTURAL PROXIMITY marker, not a convergent attractor
A/(A+xi) ~ 0.48 +/- 0.05 across all physical parameter regimes
The ~2% proximity to ln(phi) is real but precision-limited by per-realization variance
Neither coupling efficiency nor decay ratio can tune the ratio to exactly ln(phi)
This is consistent with ln(phi) emerging from the TOPOLOGY of erasure, not from specific parameter values
